properties.areaDesc: Oahu in Honolulu, HI
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 5:42PM HST until October 28 at 7:30PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The island of Oahu in Honolulu County...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM HST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding on roads, poor drainage areas, and in
streams. Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 539 PM HST, gauge reports indicated water levels in the
Waikane and Waiahole Streams have dropped. However additional
areas of showers continue to redevelop along the windward coast
between Waimanalo and Punaluu. Rain was falling at a rate of 0.5
to 1.5 inches per hour. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Kahaluu, Halawa, Waiahole, Kaneohe, Waikane, Kailua, and
Waimanalo.
properties.instruction:

flooding.

A Flood Watch remains in effect until 6 AM Thursday HST.

Kent, King, Lamb, Lubbock, Lynn, Motley, Stonewall, Terry and

properties.areaDesc: Culberson, TX
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 28 at 10:17PM CDT until October 28 at 11:15PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 1017 PM CDT /917 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated slow moving
thunderstorms continuing to produce moderate to heavy rain across the
warned area. 1 to 2 inches of rain is estimated have fallen this
evening. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams as well as other
poor drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northern Culberson County.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 28 at 10:14PM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot
of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal New Hanover County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from 8 AM EDT Thursday
through Thursday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from
9 AM to noon EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

.Persistent northeast winds and upstream tidal effects on the St John
River are slowing flow. At Deland, the river is forecast to crest
near Minor Flood Stage, then begin a slow decline through Action
Stage late week into the weekend.

forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to reach a crest of 4.0 feet. It
will then fall below flood stage late in the week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

through flooded areas.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 9:31PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and upstream tidal effects are slowing
river flow on the St Johns River at Astor. River levels are forecast
to slowly decline into the weekend but remain in Moderate Flood stage
for at least the next couple weeks.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Wednesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast to begin a gradual decline
through late week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE
